subject: Operational handover & preflight sanity for Greenline on-prem VPC
messages:
From: Samantha Jones <samantha.jones@greenline.health>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-eng@greenline.health, security@greenline.health
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Greenline on-prem VPC — operational handover kickoff

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the onboarding runbook you shared in the last meeting. The infra and security teams at Greenline are ready for the next step — operational handover for our on-prem VPC deployment. We want to run a lightweight preflight that confirms connectivity, KMS access patterns, and egress allowlist behavior before the formal cutover window.

High-level asks from our side: - A concise preflight checklist we can run with our ops team (about 60–90 minutes).
- A short list of the minimum telemetry/events Redwood needs to verify model traffic.
- Any temporary firewall/egress IPs you need whitelisted for smoke tests.

Can you propose owners and a target time this week? Prefer afternoons PT.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Jones
Head of Infrastructure, Greenline Health
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Jones <samantha.jones@greenline.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Greenline on-prem VPC — operational handover kickoff

Samantha — thanks, and +1 to afternoon. We can do a focused 75-minute preflight and confirm the items you outlined. Draft plan below (owners in parens):

1) Access sanity (15m) — verify service account SSH and API access; confirm KMS test key unwrap/unwrap (Ben).
2) Networking quick-check (20m) — validate tenant subnet reachability, NAT/egress path, and TCP health checks on 443/4433 (Marissa).
3) KV/prefix cache validation (10m) — simulate a short inference sequence to confirm KV caching behaves under your MTU/path (Karthik).
4) Telemetry smoke (15m) — ensure token-level telemetry reaches Redwood collector and sample traces are visible in the console (Naomi).
5) Contingency & rollback run-through (15m) — confirm fallback model routing and emergency egress block (Ben + Marissa).

Temporary artifacts we need from Greenline:
- An allowlist for these IPs for the smoke test: 34.201.112.45, 52.12.64.9 (we will confirm on call).
- A user/service credential with least-privilege access to hit the tenant API endpoints.

I attached a one-page checklist and a network diagram stub. If that looks good, propose Thu 17 Nov 14:00 PT (UTC-7) and we’ll send a calendar invite.

Naomi Feldman
Onboarding Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Jones <samantha.jones@greenline.health>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 12:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Greenline on-prem VPC — operational handover kickoff

Quick notes from infra ops perspective:
- KMS: we only need an RSA unwrap path for the test key; recommend using a test principal that cannot access production keys. We should record the unwrap attempt in the runbook as evidence.
- For egress: the two IPs Naomi listed are our smoke agents; I can rotate to a different pair if Greenline prefers a tighter CIDR.
- Please confirm whether Greenline uses strict MTU (some on-prem networks drop >1400). If so, Karthik, we should do an MTU-constrained trial payload.

I will prepare the short evidence checklist (log snippets + trace ids) to attach to the ticket after the test.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Deployment Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Jones <samantha.jones@greenline.health>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Greenline on-prem VPC — operational handover kickoff

Samantha — attaching a simplified network diagram (attached: greenline-network-diagram-v1.pdf) and an editable runbook checklist (redwood-runbook-checklist.xlsx). Highlights:
- Confirmed endpoints we will call for smoke: https://tenant-greenline:443/health, https://tenant-greenline:443/api/v1/model/ready
- Health checks use mutual TLS; we will verify cert chain on the call.
- If Greenline wants to restrict by CIDR rather than single IPs, propose 34.201.112.0/28 for the pilot.

Please pre-stage a service account with these minimal IAM roles: network-invoke-role, kms-unwrap-test. We will not request any write-level keys during the preflight.

If Thu 2pm PT is still good, we are confirmed on our side.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Deployment Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Jones <samantha.jones@greenline.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, security@greenline.health
Date: Thu, 18 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Greenline on-prem VPC — operational handover kickoff (Confirmed)

Samantha — thanks for staging the service account and the CIDR. Confirming run order for today’s 14:00 PT preflight:

14:00 — 14:15 Access sanity (Ben) — confirm SSH/service principal & KMS unwrap test
14:15 — 14:35 Network quick-check (Marissa) — subnet reachability, MTU note, mutual TLS handshake
14:35 — 14:45 KV/cache smoke (Karthik) — short seq, check latency and cache hits
14:45 — 15:00 Telemetry & trace verification (Naomi) — sample trace ids: GH-TR-1114 / GH-TR-1115 will be generated and posted to the Drive link
15:00 — 15:15 Contingency review and next steps (Ben + Marissa)

Post-call deliverables (we will upload to Drive and to HubSpot GH-39472):
- Evidence bundle: network logs (pcap-lite), KMS unwrap logs, sample traces, and final signed checklist.
- Suggested follow-up: soft cutover window (one-hour) if all green.

Thanks all — see you on the call.

Naomi Feldman
Onboarding Manager, Redwood Inference
